abstract.p: Insufficient sleep is common among first-year university students and may impair the cognitive processes required to solve quantitative problems. This fictitious study examined the association between self-reported sleep duration in the week before an examination and performance on a statistics midterm exam. A total of 156 first-year students completed a sleep diary for seven nights and a brief questionnaire on study habits. Students who slept less than six hours per night obtained lower exam scores than those who slept seven hours or more, after adjusting for prior academic achievement and weekly study time. The association followed a dose-response pattern. These findings suggest that sleep hygiene programs could complement academic support during examination periods, although longitudinal designs are needed to establish the direction of the effect.
